_comment: LSDn real-landscape validation manifest --
the END-TO-END PER-PIXEL tier. Small, TRACKED file; no raster is ever committed.
WHAT THIS MEASURES, AND WHAT IT IS NOT. It compares (a) lsdtt3's PER-PIXEL LSDn
basin-mean erosion rate against (c) OCTOPUS's published EBEL. That mixes THREE
independent things: the LSDn scaling-kernel residual (pinned separately by test
L12, which is DEM-free), the per-pixel-vs-lumped difference (pinned separately
by test L13, and a scientific RESULT, not an error), and the DEM difference
(COP30 here vs whatever OCTOPUS used, plus delineation). It is therefore a
MONITORING BAND, NOT AN ORACLE: attribute it with L12 and L13, do not read it
as an accuracy figure, and NEVER tune anything to shrink it.
NO DUPLICATED DATA. sample_table points at the St tier's OWN table: every
quantity lsdtt-cosmo-tool consumes (position, Be10_CONC, uncertainty) is
identical between the two tiers, so there is exactly one copy of each measured
concentration in the repository. Only the published TARGET differs, and that is
supplied by published_erate_override below from the tracked, harvested
octopus_lsdn_point_reference.csv (EBEL, mm/kyr).
description: LSDn (Lifton, Sato & Dunai 2014) tier of the Dethier et al. (2014) Front Range dataset. SAME basins, SAME DEM footprint, SAME run knobs and the SAME sample table as 'dethier2014' -- the only differences are scaling_scheme: lsdn and the published target, which becomes OCTOPUS's EBEL (LSDn) instead of EBE_* (Stone/Lal).

published_reference.citation: Dethier, D.P., Ouimet, W., Bierman, P.R., Rood, D.H., Balco, G. (2014), Geology 42(2), 167-170.
published_reference.calculator: OCTOPUS v2.3(4) EBEL = LSDn. NOT a CAIRN recalculation: CAIRN implements only time-independent Stone/Lal (Saktura et al. 2025, GChron 7:113), so OCTOPUS reduces each basin to (CENTR_LAT, ATM_PRESS) and feeds those two scalars to the Balco et al. (2008) v3 point calculator via RIVERSAND. EBEL is that POINT result, not a per-pixel average -- which is precisely why this tier is a monitoring band and the DEM-free L12 test is the kernel oracle.

_comment: Regression targets (concentration, uncertainty, standard, denudation rate)
are harvested from OCTOPUS, NOT scraped from the paper and NOT invented.
OCTOPUS recalculates every rate with CAIRN -- the same algorithm
lsdtt-cosmo-tool implements -- so these are a NEAR-CAIRN oracle, not
bit-exact (see residual_expectation).
octopus_source.cql_note: Filter with CQL_FILTER, not bbox: the OCTOPUS server throws a ProjectionException on the WFS 2.0.0 bbox parameter.
octopus_source.scaling_scheme: LSDn -- EBEL / EBEL_INT / EBEL_EXT (mm/kyr), field names confirmed 2026-07-26 against the live WFS DescribeFeatureType on be10-denude:crn_int_basins. EBELNS is the no-TOPOGRAPHIC-shielding control. lsdtt-cosmo-tool is run with scaling_scheme: lsdn to match.

_comment: MEASURED-THEN-RECORDED, and DECOMPOSED rather than interpreted.
SIGN. This file and the summary use 100*(lsdtt3 - published)/published. L12 and L13
publish the OPPOSITE sign, 100*(octopus - lsdtt3)/lsdtt3. Convert before combining.
In THIS convention the components are:
(1) kernel, L12 (b vs c), on lsdtt3's own P0 -- which is what the CLI uses:  -6.14 %
(L12 prints +6.54 %). With Balco's LSDn-calibrated P0 instead: -4.16 %
(L12 prints +4.34 %). The CLI cannot switch P0, so -6.14 % is the term here.
(2) per-pixel vs lumped, L13 (a vs b): -0.53 % median, -0.83 % mean, t matched.
(3) config, carried from the St tier: ERA40 rather than NCEP -0.64 %, and
topographic shielding ignored +0.70 %.
=> matched-age expectation approximately -6.6 %.
(4) TIME -- the term that moves this tier off that expectation. run_params keeps the
CLI default sample_age_yr = 0, i.e. the MODERN (2010) geomagnetic field, whereas
EBEL is Balco v3 time-averaged over the erosional timescale Gamma/eps (12-38 kyr
for these rates, from L12's t_yr column). The Holocene field was STRONGER than
today, so the time-averaged production is LOWER: from the frozen L13 artefact,
basin-mean LSDn production at t = 0 is +27.5 % above t = 5000 yr and +13.9 % above
t = 20000 yr on these same 50 basins. That raises the measured band by roughly
+11 points relative to (1)-(3), which is what is seen.
MEASURED DIRECTLY on dethier2014, not argued: repeating the identical run at
sample_age_yr = 5000 / 15000 / 20000 gives mean -16.1 / -9.3 / -7.0 % on the same
12 basins, bracketing the -6.6 % expectation at the ages the nuclide integrates.
This is a stated property of the CONFIGURATION, not a defect of the kernel, and
it is NOT to be tuned away. Whether the frozen tier should instead carry a
matched sample_age_yr is a decision for review, not for a test author.
residual_expectation.band: MEASURED 2026-07-26, first accepted run: 12 delineation_reliable basins: min +2.47, max +9.41, mean +4.51, median +4.28 % (sign 100*(lsdtt3 - EBEL)/EBEL). Excluded: S169WTS036 (+101.7 %) and S169WTS032, both 0.07 km2, below the 0.225 km2 snap footprint.
residual_expectation.attribute_residual_to: kernel (L12) + per-pixel/lumped (L13) + config + the dominant sample_age_yr=0 vs Gamma/eps time term; a MONITORING BAND, not an accuracy figure.

dem.dem_source_note: Keyless. Driven through the lsdtt-fetch-raster CLI, which retrieves and clips Copernicus GLO-30 from AWS Open Data (dem_source: cop30_aws) or Microsoft Planetary Computer (dem_source: planetary_computer) with NO account or API key. Set dem_source to planetary_computer to use the PC STAC mirror instead.
dem.target_epsg_note: UTM 13N (EPSG:32613) for the Colorado Front Range; matches OCTOPUS PROJEPSGID for these S169 basins. The cosmo CLIs require a PROJECTED CRS, so the DEM is warped to UTM at fetch time.
dem.resolution_choice_note: COP30 (30 m) vs the DEM used in the OCTOPUS/CAIRN recalculation is a DOCUMENTED, attributable difference in the validation (DEM resolution + product), not a bug -- record it alongside the production-scheme residual in the summary.

bounding_box._comment: Union of the 14 pilot basins' OCTOPUS outline footprints, padded ~0.02 deg. Covers the whole cluster in one modest DEM.

_comment: IDENTICAL to the St tier's run_params (same threshold_contributing_pixels and
snap_search_radius_pixels, so the SAME basins are delineated the SAME way and the
St and LSDn summaries are directly differenceable), plus scaling_scheme: lsdn.
run_cosmo_validation.py forwards these verbatim into the parameter file.
self_consistent_age: true (added 2026-07-27, Simon's decision) makes this tier
AGE-MATCHED to EBEL. The tool now solves the sample age and the erosion rate
together at t = Gamma_sp/eps, which is the CRONUScalc / Balco v3 convention EBEL
was computed under. Previously this ran at the CLI default sample_age_yr = 0
(modern field), and that mismatch alone was ~+11 points of the band -- its
largest single term. sample_age_yr is left at 0 as the ITERATION'S STARTING
GUESS, not as the reported age; the converged age is written per sample to
self_consistent_t_yr in the tool's output CSV.
This does NOT turn the band into an oracle. Removing the age term leaves the
kernel residual, the per-pixel-vs-lumped term and the DEM/delineation
difference, all still mixed -- see residual_expectation. NEVER tune to shrink it.
Swap the published comparison target from EBE_* (Stone/Lal) to EBEL (LSDn)
WITHOUT copying the sample table. The source is the tracked, WFS-harvested
point reference; a missing file, a missing row, a non-positive rate or an
unexpected implied density is a HARD FAILURE in the harness, never a skip.
published_erate_override.units: mm_kyr; converted with OCTOPUS's own density EBE_GCMYR/(EBE_MMKYR*1e-4) = 2.650 g/cm3
